details:
RedRoute: Martian Survival & Exploration Route-Planning Framework

1. Project Overview & Inspiration

The RedRoute project is an interactive, web-based mission planning and spatial decision-support application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. As humanity looks toward crewed exploration and permanent settlement on Mars, mission planners and future astronauts face complex environmental hurdles. Choosing a habitat location or charting a rover traverse requires balancing conflicting variables—such as surface elevation, local terrain ruggedness, thermal stability, proximity to sub-surface water ice potential, and radiation shielding.

Inspired by NASA’s rich history of planetary exploration and data from missions like MGS MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter), RedRoute bridges raw scientific datasets with an intuitive, interactive visualization platform. It empowers users to analyze potential landing sites, simulate rover paths, and evaluate planetary habitability metrics in real-time.

2. Key Features & Architecture

RedRoute is engineered as a lightweight, high-performance single-file web applicationdesigned for universal accessibility across devices without heavy backend infrastructure bottlenecks. Core modules include:

  • Interactive 3D Mars Globe & Surface Viewer: Powered by WebGL/Three.js frameworks, users can dynamically rotate and explore the Martian globe, inspect interior planetary layers (crust, mantle, core), and view high-fidelity 3D models of rovers and space suits situated on the Martian terrain.
  • Landing Site Evaluation Planner: The application integrates a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) matrix covering nine prominent Martian regions (including Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, and Valles Marineris). Users can dynamically adjust mission priorities—such as prioritizing water access, minimizing terrain slope hazards, or optimizing thermal conditions—to automatically re-rank landing sites.
  • Live NASA Data Integration: RedRoute connects directly with public NASA/JPL APIs and services. It fetches live MOLA global topographic hillshade map tiles, queries the NASA Image and Video Library for real-time mission imagery from the Perseverance rover, and samples numerical elevation and slope data from the PDS Geosciences Node.
  • Accessibility & Multi-Language Support: To foster global inclusivity, the platform features built-in text-to-speech tools, full-screen toggles, customizable typography sizing, and an instant English-to-Bangla translation engine.

3. Technical Implementation & Data Sources

  • Frontend Stack: Built using native HTML5, modern CSS3, and JavaScript, leveraging modular ES6 architecture for optimal execution speed.
  • Rendering Engine: Utilizes Three.js for hardware-accelerated 3D graphics rendering of planetary spheres, rovers, and astronaut models.
  • Planetary Datasets: Grounded in peer-reviewed planetary science datasets from NASA and the USGS, utilizing MOLA elevation models and official planetary fact sheets to maintain rigorous scientific accuracy.

4. Impact & Future Scope

RedRoute serves as both an educational gateway for students and a functional proof-of-concept for preliminary mission planning. By translating complex orbital telemetry and altimetry data into a gamified, interactive decision-making tool, the project demonstrates how localized edge computing and web technologies can make deep-space exploration data accessible, engaging, and practically useful for future space pioneers.
